sentences.text: Petitioner is challenging the proceedings in C.C.No.76 of 2023 on the files of the Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Chottanikkara, which arises out of Crime No.376 of 2021of Chottanikkara Police Station.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate's Court, Chottanikkara
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
According to the prosecution, the first accused had stolen the gold ornaments weighing 9.7 sovereigns valued at Rs.4,00,000/- and the same was entrusted with the 2 nd accused thereby committing the offences under Sections 381, 411, 414 and 461 and 201 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.
I have heard Sri.Saijo Hassan, the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Smt.Sreeja V., the learned Public Prosecutor.

sentences.text: Though the petitioner contends that he has been roped into the crime as a person who received the stolen goods, he had no knowledge that the goods were stolen and there are no materials to indicate that he received the goods knowing that it was stolen.

4. Notwithstanding the above contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner, I am of the view that this is not a matter which can be interfered with under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.

It is settled principle that when disputed facts arises, the court cannot exercise its inherent jurisdiction to quash the CRL.MC NO. 6769 OF 2024 2024:KER:70355 proceedings, that too at the initial stage.

If the petitioner has a case that the records collected by the Investigating Officer would not make out any of the offences alleged against the him, certainly, he is at liberty to approach the jurisdictional court with an application for discharge.
In the nature of contentions urged, I am not inclined to exercise the inherent power to quash the proceedings.
Therefore, reserving the liberty of the petitioner to apply for discharge, if entitled to under law, this Crl.M.C. is dismissed.

Sd/-
